_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC SOS Fade — labels, groups, plain-English descriptions, the 'essentials' (core) flag, conditional visibility (show_if), toggle option labels, and tuning guides. Read by the command-center scanner (strategies/python/<pkg>/<pkg>.meta.json) and overlaid onto the schema built from SosFadeConfig. UI ONLY: it never touches a trade decision or the source hash, so editing it needs no re-parity — but DO click Scan Strategies after editing. Param order here is the canonical UI order. Every show_if below was verified against the code, not assumed: exec_fvg_deep_only deliberately has NO condition (it still filters which FVGs qualify when Require FVG is off), and div_rsi_len/div_pivot_len have none either (they drive the divergence that ARMS the setup, which show_div does not gate — show_div only gates the veto and the live DIV flag). LABELS AND DESCRIPTIONS ARE SHARED WITH THE PINE (2026-08-02): every `label` here is byte-identical to that input's title in indicators/strategies/mpc_strategy.pine (minus Pine's leading '   ↳ ' indent marker), and every `desc` is that input's tooltip verbatim. One parameter, one name, one explanation, two UIs. Change a label or a desc and change the Pine in the same commit, or the two panels start teaching different things. The ONE allowed deviation is a suffix stating a fact true only of THIS runner — exec_conf_sz carries '(not supported)' because the Sniper-Zone entry is Pine-only. COPY STYLE (2026-08-10, Aaron's call): every desc is SHORT and PLAIN — what the setting does, what each choice means, and the one fact that changes the decision. No measurement dumps, no trade counts, no R figures, no dates, no file references: the strategy detail page is for reading, and the evidence behind a default lives in this package's CLAUDE.md and its optimization doc. Same rule for `edge` and `steps`.
edge: It trades reversals, but only once the market has proved the turn. First price runs the stops past a recent high or low. Then structure breaks the other way, which is the confirmation. Then it waits for a deep pullback and leaves a limit order sitting there — it never chases. Most of the money comes from the part of the trade that is left to run.

steps.label: 01 · Arm
steps.title: Something runs out of steam
steps.detail: Price runs the stops past a recent high or low. That is what puts a setup on the watchlist. A momentum divergence at an extreme can do it too, but that is off by default.

steps.label: 02 · Confirm
steps.title: Structure breaks the other way
steps.detail: The market breaks back the other way soon after. Without that the setup is only a guess, so it never arms.

steps.label: 03 · Zone
steps.title: Wait for the pullback
steps.detail: Price comes back deep into the move and a gap left behind sits in the same place. A limit order rests there and waits to be filled. It is never a chase.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Let it run
steps.detail: Touching the first target moves the stop to breakeven, so the trade can no longer lose. By default nothing is banked early — the whole position rides out on the trailing stop.

params.name: exec_arm_div
params.label: Arm on RSI divergence
params.desc: Lets a momentum divergence start a setup. If this and the sweep trigger are both off, nothing ever trades.

params.name: exec_arm_sweep
params.label: Arm on liquidity sweep
params.desc: Lets a run on the stops past a recent high or low start a setup.

params.name: aplus_window
params.label: Max time: sweep → SOS (minutes)
params.desc: How long a stop run stays valid while it waits for structure to confirm. 4320 = 3 days.
guide: Only fresh signals count — fewer setups
An old signal can still trigger days later

params.name: exec_aplus
params.label: Trade A+ setups
params.desc: On = the main reversal setup trades normally. Off = it never fires, so you can read the B leg on its own.

params.name: exec_bleg
params.label: Trade B-Leg setups
params.desc: Adds a second setup: when a reversal never gets its pullback, this waits for the pullback to arrive late and buys it there.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: Lets long setups trade. Off = shorts only.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: Lets short setups trade. Off = longs only.

params.name: exec_req_fvg
params.label: Require an FVG in the zone
params.desc: On = only trade when there is a gap in the pullback zone. Off = trade the pullback on its own.

params.name: exec_nogap_arm
params.label: ↳ No-FVG entries need
params.desc: Which no-gap setups may still trade when a gap is not required. Any = all of them. Sweep + RSI div = only the ones with both signals behind the turn. Lab only — this setting is not on the TradingView chart.

params.name: exec_poi_source
params.label: Zone the entry reads (lab only)
params.desc: Which kind of zone the entry price is read off. FVG is the shipped rule. The order-block modes were tested and did not earn their place; they are kept so anyone can re-check that. Lab only — only FVG exists on the TradingView chart.

params.name: exec_ob_deepen
params.label: Order block deeper than the entry → rest on the block
params.desc: On = when an order block sits deeper than the entry, move the order down onto it. A better price and a tighter stop, paid for in trades that never fill. Tested and rejected. Lab only.

params.name: exec_fvg_deep_only
params.label: Gap must sit fully past 0.5
params.desc: On = the whole gap must sit in the deep half of the pullback. Stricter, so fewer setups.

params.name: exec_fvg_pre_zone
params.label: Gap must pre-date the zone
params.desc: On = the gap only counts if it was already there before price pulled back this far.

params.name: exec_fib_overlap
params.label: Gap on a fib → enter on the fib
params.desc: On = when a fib level sits inside the gap, rest the order on that level instead of at the gap's edge.

params.name: exec_fib_deep_edge
params.label: Floating gap → its own deep edge
params.desc: For a gap holding no fib level and sitting deeper than 0.618, rest the order at its far edge.

params.name: exec_fib_nearest
params.label: Floating gap → nearest fib (either side)
params.desc: Same gap as the rule above, but rest on whichever fib level is closest, above or below.

params.name: exec_deep_fib
params.label: Floating gap → nearest fib shallower
params.desc: The older one-sided version of the two rules above, kept so old results still reproduce.

params.name: exec_conf_sz
params.label: Allow Sniper Zone as entry confirmation (not supported)
params.desc: Not supported in this bot — leave it off. Turning it on changes nothing on a lab run, and the TradingView comparison refuses an export taken with it on.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. The stop distance sets the position size, so a tighter stop buys a bigger position at the same risk.
guide: Smaller swings, slower growth
Bigger swings — 10% is already aggressive

params.name: exec_sl_level
params.label: Stop fib level (deep side of 0.5)
params.desc: How far back the stop sits. 1.0 is the widest and safest; the tighter levels can put the stop almost on the entry.

params.name: exec_sl_custom
params.label: Custom stop fib level
params.desc: Type your own stop level, used when the setting above is Custom. Deeper, towards 1.0, is the safe direction: a wider stop and a smaller position. Shallower than 0.886 is the dangerous half — turn on the minimum stop distance first. Lab only.
guide: Tighter stop, bigger position, less room to be right
Wider stop, smaller position, more room

params.name: exec_sl_deep
params.label: Entries at 0.786 or deeper stop at 1.0
params.disable_note: No effect — the stop is already 1.0, so both states place it in the same spot.
params.desc: On = an entry filling at 0.786 or deeper puts its stop right back at the start of the move, giving it more room.

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Stop buffer beyond the level (ticks)
params.desc: Extra room beyond the stop level, in ticks, so a wick through it does not take you out.
guide: Stop sits exactly on the level
More room for wicks, wider risk per trade

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Skip a setup whose stop sits closer to the entry than the floor below.

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: Minimum stop floor (unit = mode above)
params.desc: The floor itself, in whatever unit the setting above uses. Higher refuses more setups.
guide: Almost nothing is refused
Refuses real trades, not just dangerous ones

params.name: exec_be_arm_r
params.label: Any trade moves to breakeven at (R)
guide: Off — the stop holds until a rung is touched
Protects every trade earlier
params.desc: When ANY trade's stop moves to protect it, measured on how far price has gone its way as a multiple of the trade's own risk. -1 (default) is off, which is the shipped behaviour: the only thing that moves the stop is price TOUCHING a rung on the ladder, so a trade can run a full R in profit, turn around and pay the full loss with nothing having happened — the re-entry short of 2020-11-04 did exactly that at 1.016R with its nearest rung at 1.25R. MEASURED 2026-08-25 over 6.6 years on 246 trades: every setting tested LOST money against leaving it off — 139.09R off, against 99.92R at 1.00, 71.20R at 0.75 and 51.55R at 0.50. At 1.00 it rescued 17 trades worth +17.07R and destroyed 15 worth -54.49R, one of them a +16.48R winner cut to +0.35R. Win rate rose 58% to 69% while the money fell by two thirds, which is the fingerprint of cutting winners. Lab only, and it is kept as a recorded dead end.
params.warn: MEASURED WORSE at every setting tested — 139.09R down to 99.92R at best. It cuts the winners that carry the book.

params.name: exec_be_keep_r
params.label: Protected stop keeps (R) of risk
guide: All the way to breakeven
Leaves more risk in the market
params.desc: How FAR the stop moves when the row above arms it. 0 (default) is all the way to breakeven. A positive number leaves that share of the trade's own entry risk in the market, so a trade that is protected and then turns around pays part of the loss rather than none of it. MEASURED 2026-08-25: it is the least bad version and still worse than off — 118.99R at 1.00 and 108.12R at 0.75 against 139.09R off, and at 0.75 the worst drawdown got WORSE (60.21% against 53.68%). Must be under 1 — at 1 the stop lands back on the entry stop and does nothing while reading as switched on. Does nothing on its own. Lab only.
params.warn: MEASURED WORSE than off — 118.99R at best against 139.09R, and at 0.75 it deepened the drawdown.

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: TP1 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the first target banks. 0 = bank nothing and ride it all. Touching it still moves the stop to breakeven.
guide: More size left for the runner
Bank more early, smaller runner

params.name: exec_tp2_pct
params.label: TP2 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the second target banks. 0 = bank nothing. Touching it still lifts the stop and hands the rest to the trail.
guide: Bigger runner
Bank more at TP2, smaller runner

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer (ticks)
params.desc: How far past the entry the breakeven stop sits, so a scratch still covers costs. Read only when the buffer mode is set to ticks.
guide: True breakeven
Locks in more, stopped out sooner

params.name: exec_be_buf_mode
params.label: Breakeven buffer mode
params.desc: What the breakeven stop's cushion is measured in. Ticks is one fixed distance on every trade. The other two size it to what the trade is actually risking, and the third also guarantees the exit clears what the trade has cost.
guide: Ticks — same distance whatever the trade risks
Fraction of stop + cost — scales, and never exits at a loss

params.name: exec_be_buf_r
params.label: Breakeven buffer (fraction of stop)
params.desc: The cushion as a share of what the trade risked. 0.20 is one fifth of the stop. Only read when the buffer mode is not ticks.
guide: Close to breakeven
Locks in more, stopped out sooner

params.name: exec_be_cost_margin_r
params.label: Breakeven cost margin (fraction of stop)
params.desc: How far the stop clears the trade's own costs by. 0 exits exactly flat after costs; anything above banks a little. Only read in the cost-covering mode.
guide: Flat after costs
Keeps more, stopped out sooner

params.name: exec_be_cap_pct
params.label: Breakeven buffer cap (% of the way to the target)
params.unit: % of the distance to the target
params.desc: The stop can never sit further than this share of the way from the entry to the target that moved it. At 100 it would sit on the target and close the trade there instead of protecting it.
guide: Stop stays well short of the target
Stop crowds the target

params.name: exec_be_cost_conflict
params.label: When cost exceeds the cap
params.desc: What to do on a trade held so long that its financing alone is further from the entry than the cap allows. Hold leaves the original stop where it is. Clamp moves it anyway and accepts a known small loss.
guide: Hold — never exit at a knowing loss
Clamp — smaller loss than the full stop

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the stop follows the trade once the second target is hit. Fixed step is a plain dollar grid; structure parks it at the last swing.
guide: Fixed step — simplest, and the worst of the three
Structure + ratchet — keeps more of each run

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: How many ticks beyond the last swing the trailing stop sits, so a wick through it does not clip you.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

params.name: exec_trail_pct
params.label: Runner ratchet step (% of price)
params.desc: How big each trailing step is, as a percent of price rather than dollars, so it means the same at any price.
guide: Too small — cuts winners short
Too big — barely does anything

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: The step size in dollars. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit. TP1 is tight and can scratch the trade; breakeven gives it the most room.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

params.name: exec_scale_in
params.label: Add to the runner (scale in)
params.desc: Buys more once the trailing stop is already locking in profit; Off means the position never grows after entry. The add is sized so that being stopped out costs at most the profit already locked in, so it can shrink a winner but never create a loser.

params.name: exec_scale_mode
params.label: Where it adds
params.desc: Where it adds. Trail buys at market the moment the trailing stop moves up; BOS retest waits for the next break of structure and rests an order at the level that broke.
guide: Trail — the measured choice; adds most often and makes the money
BOS retest — waits for a pullback that often never comes; loses money outside 2020

params.name: exec_scale_max_adds
params.label: How many times it may add
params.desc: The most times one trade may add. It only adds again once the trailing stop has moved up since the last add, so a stalling trade gets nothing.
guide: Fewer adds — smaller position, shallower drawdown
More adds — bigger runners, more given back

params.name: exec_scale_cap_x
params.label: Biggest add, as a multiple of the original size
params.desc: A ceiling on each add, as a multiple of the size the trade opened with. 1.0 means an add can never be bigger than the original position.
guide: Lower — this is the drawdown lever; 0.5 is the measured best
Higher — more return bought with much more drawdown, and more gap exposure

params.name: exec_scale_tp_mode
params.label: Where the adds take profit
params.desc: Where the added lots bank. Ride leaves them on the trailing stop with the rest of the trade, which is how every run before 2026-08-19 behaved. The other three rest them at the nearest level of that kind price has not already taken, and only when it sits beyond the newest add, so every lot banks in profit. It moves the ADDS only — the base trade's stop and partials are untouched.
guide: Ride — the default, and measured best (194.15R); the adds earn on the few trades that run a long way
Prev week H/L — costs 25.64R (168.51R), OUTSIDE this strategy's own 15.06R noise
Prev day / H4 — worse again (157.57R / 146.09R), and worse the more often the level gets hit

params.name: exec_time_stop_mode
params.label: Time stop
params.desc: Closes a trade open longer than the hours below. Before TP1 only fires while the trade has never reached the first target.
guide: Off — the clock never closes a trade
Always — the clock closes winners too

params.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
params.label: Time stop (hours)
params.desc: How long a trade may stay open, in hours, weekends included. About 24 to 40 hours all give the same answer.
guide: Cuts winners as well as losers
Fires on almost nothing

params.name: exec_close_opp_sos
params.label: Close on opposite SOS
params.desc: On = close the trade early if structure breaks back the other way. Off = let the stop or a target resolve it.

params.name: exec_secondary
params.label: Secondary re-entries
params.desc: Adds a second entry off a FASTER chart than the strategy trades — the fill clock set below, 5 minutes by default: once the first trade is safe at breakeven and price falls back into the zone, it re-enters for the same targets. On by default. MEASURED over 7.9 years on the settings that now ship: 54 re-entries, worth +13.9R on top of the first trades' +206.2R, and the first trades are untouched to the decimal. It is bought with drawdown — the worst peak-to-trough goes from 51.8% to 60.4% — and it leans hard on one trade, which is why it is sized at half. Lab only, and slower to run than a plain backtest.

params.name: exec_sec_trigger
params.label: What triggers a re-entry
params.desc: What has to happen before a re-entry places its order. FVG in zone (default) needs no structure event at all — while the setup is alive and price is back in the zone, it rests the order at the SAME fair-value-gap price the first trade would have used. Structure shift is the original rule: a break of structure on the fill clock, then an order at a 38.2% pullback of that move. MEASURED: the shift confirms late. On 29 October 2025 it did not confirm until an hour after the low, its order missed by $8 and price ran a hundred points without it; a gap sat in the zone and price traded into it an hour earlier. Reclaim Entry is the only one of the three built for a trade that LOST: the first trade is stopped at the deep edge of the entry band, price does not go on to break the move, and instead comes back up through that level — an order then waits AT the level for the retest, stopping at the far end of the move. Because those two levels sit close together the risk is a fraction of the first trade's, so the same cash buys a much bigger position. It reads its OWN four settings below rather than the shared ones, so it means the same thing whether it runs alone or alongside the gap. MEASURED: waiting for the retest earned +43R over 7.9 years while chasing the reclaim earned nothing, so the wait is the whole edge. The fourth choice runs the gap and the reclaim TOGETHER. That is safe because they cover opposite outcomes — a first trade either reaches breakeven or is stopped out, never both — so they can never want the same setup. MEASURED over 7.9 years: 107 re-entries between them, none sharing a setup and none overlapping another in time, and the two together are exactly the two apart. It requires the gap half set to Breakeven and the reclaim half to Stopped only, and refuses any other pairing. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_zone_deep
params.label: Secondary zone — deep edge
params.desc: How deep into the retrace the re-entry may still arm, as a fib ratio. 0.886 (default) is the entry band's own edge. 1.0 is the start of the leg, which lets it arm while price has closed BEYOND the band — the state a swept stop leaves behind. It does not move the re-entry's stop. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_zone_shallow
params.label: Secondary zone — shallow edge
params.desc: The shallow end of that same zone, as a fib ratio. 0.618 (default) is the entry band's edge. A smaller number lets the re-entry arm after price has already reclaimed part of the move — more chances, at a worse price relative to the targets. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_max_wait_bars
params.label: Cancel a resting re-entry after (fill-clock bars)
guide: Never cancels — it waits for the setup to die
Gives up on the order sooner
params.desc: How long a resting re-entry order may wait unfilled before it is taken off the book. 0 (default) never cancels, which is the shipped behaviour: the order rests at its price until the setup that armed it dies. Counted in FILL-CLOCK bars, so it moves with the fill clock above — at a 5-minute clock, 144 is 12 hours. Once cancelled, that setup cannot place the order again; a fresh break of structure arms a new one. MEASURED 2026-08-23 over 6.6 years: 61 of 90 re-entry orders fill inside 30 minutes, and every cutoff of 6 hours or less loses money because the 6-to-12-hour band is the best in the book (4 wins from 5, +11.25R). Past 12 hours the book has never won — 8 orders, 8 losses, worth +8.00R to cancel, on 8 trades. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_risk_pct
params.label: Re-entry risk (% of the first trade's)
params.desc: How much a re-entry risks, as a percentage of what a first trade risks. 50 (default) is half; 100 is the same. It changes the SIZE only — entry, stop and targets are identical, so the R figure a re-entry reports does not move at all and must be scaled by this number before it is compared with a first trade's. MEASURED over 7.9 years: the re-entries add 6.9R at a quarter, 13.9R at half, 20.9R at three-quarters and 27.8R at full weight, and the worst peak-to-trough goes 56.2 / 60.4 / 64.4 / 68.1 per cent against 51.8 with them off — a straight line with no natural stopping place, so half was chosen because one trade is three quarters of the whole leg's profit. Zero is refused: use the on/off switch instead. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_req_div
params.label: Re-entry needs a divergence
params.desc: Whether a re-entry also needs a live RSI divergence on the 15-minute chart, on top of the setup still being alive and price being back in the zone. Not needed (default). It is NOT the same question as what arms the first trade — the bot ships finding its trades from liquidity sweeps, so the divergence is usually absent and requiring it stops re-entries firing at all: MEASURED over the year to 2026-08-18, zero re-entries with it required. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_req_m1_dir
params.label: Fill-clock trend must agree
params.desc: On = a re-entry only arms while the structure on the FILL CLOCK (the faster feed set below, 5 minutes by default) is already pointing the trade's way. This is the "has structure shifted against me" test on the lower timeframe. MEASURED: it drops 2 of 7 re-entries and does not filter the one full loss. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_be_at
params.label: Re-entry moves to breakeven at
params.desc: When a re-entry's stop jumps to breakeven. TP1 (default) is the same rule the first trade uses. TP2 holds the original stop for longer, giving the trade room to breathe. MEASURED: TP2 is WORSE — the three trades it saved from a breakeven scratch each became a full loss instead. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_once_per_setup
params.label: One re-entry per primary
params.desc: How often one setup may be re-entered. On = once. Off = once per signal on the fill clock, which is what once let a single setup be re-entered twice about an hour and a half apart. It resets on a fresh break of structure. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_max_per_setup
params.label: ↳ How many re-entries per setup
params.desc: Read only when One re-entry per primary is ON. How many times one setup may be re-entered before it is done. A re-entry that is STOPPED OUT still ends the setup whatever this says, so raising it only lets a setup be re-tried after a scratch. MEASURED over 6.6 years: 2, 3, 5 and unlimited all produce the same book — only one setup ever offered a second re-entry, and it lost. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_rest_and_leave
params.label: Rest the re-entry order and leave it
params.desc: Once the re-entry's order is placed it stays there, at the price it was placed at. It only comes off if the setup that placed it dies, the trade fills, or the leg is finished. Off re-decides the order from scratch on every bar, so any one condition closing pulls it back off the book — which is what made the order need re-checking every minute.

params.name: exec_sec_fill_tf_min
params.label: Re-entry fill clock (minutes)
params.desc: Which bars the backtest fills the re-entry's resting order against. It changes how accurate the test is, not how the strategy trades — live, the broker fills at the price that trades. A coarser setting fills you worse than really happened, so the result reads worse than it is. Smaller is more faithful and much slower to load.

params.name: exec_rec_require
params.label: Reclaim needs the first trade to have…
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.
params.desc: What the first trade on this setup must have done before Reclaim Entry may re-enter. Stopped only (default) is the whole point of that trigger — it re-enters a setup whose first trade was stopped out at the deep edge. It is separate from the shared setting above so the gap trigger and the reclaim can run together wanting opposite things of the same trade; when they do, this must stay on Stopped only and the shared one on Breakeven, because those are the only two that cannot both be true of one setup. Lab only.

params.name: exec_rec_stop
params.label: Reclaim stop sits at
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.
params.desc: Where Reclaim Entry's stop goes. Only these two, because the reclaim enters at a fixed price and a swing on the fill clock can land on either side of it — a stop that is sometimes above and sometimes below the thing it protects is not a stop, so the fill-clock anchors are refused rather than substituted. 1.0 is the default and is the reason the trigger exists: the start of the move sits a median 0.43 of the original risk past the deep edge, so the same cash buys a much bigger position. Lab only.

params.name: exec_rec_tp_r
params.label: Reclaim's first target, in R
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.
guide: Banks sooner, gives up the runs
Waits for a bigger move, more of them fail
params.desc: Where Reclaim Entry's first target sits, as a multiple of its own risk. -1 uses the halfway fib instead, like the first trade. MEASURED over 7.9 years and the ladder matters as much as the number: taking the whole position off at 3x made 7,225x, where banking half at 1.25x — the gap trigger's ladder — made 3,111x, which is worse than taking no re-entry at all. A re-entry priced this tight has to be allowed to pay for the ones that fail. MEASURED 2026-08-27, nine targets replayed over 47 reclaims: 2.00x 13.00R, 2.50x 19.50R, 3.00x 25.00R, 3.25x 29.50R, 3.50x 29.50R, then a cliff — 3.75x 14.75R and 4.00x 13.95R. 3.25x is the default: moving up from 3.00x changed no trade's outcome at all, the same 18 winners simply carried further, and it keeps twice the margin 3.50x has before the cliff for the same money. Lab only.

params.name: exec_rec_tp1_pct
params.label: Reclaim banks at its first target (%)
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.
guide: Keeps a runner, gives up certainty
Takes it all off at the target
params.desc: How much of Reclaim Entry comes off at its first target. 100 (default) is the whole position, leaving no runner, and that is the configuration the numbers on the setting above were measured at. -1 inherits the shared first-target size. MEASURED: taking only half off measured strictly worse, twice. Lab only.

params.name: exec_rec_entry_mode
params.label: Reclaim enters
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.
guide: Waits for price to come back
Takes the next price, whatever it is
params.desc: How a Reclaim Entry gets in. Retest (default) is the shipped path: price sweeps the first trade's stop, trades back through that level, and an order then RESTS at the level waiting for price to come back to it. Market takes the next fill-clock bar instead — it cannot miss the move, but the stop does NOT move with it, so the risk is wider, the position smaller, and the target (a multiple of that risk) sits further away in price. MEASURED 2026-08-24 over 6.6 years: market entry took the reclaim book 30.00R down to 23.11R and drawdown 43% up to 54%, and it was worse again at a wider or tighter target. It rescues only 3 trades that never got a fill. Lab only.
params.warn: Measured WORSE than the default over 6.6 years — 30.00R down to 23.11R, with drawdown 43% up to 54%.

params.name: exec_rec_be_r
params.label: Reclaim moves to breakeven at (R)
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.
guide: Off — the stop holds until the target
Protects the trade earlier
params.desc: When a Reclaim Entry's stop moves to protect the trade, measured on how far price has gone its way as a multiple of the trade's own risk. -1 (default) is off, which is the shipped behaviour: the stop does not move at all until the first target, and because the whole position comes off there a reclaim that runs most of the way and turns around pays the full loss. MEASURED 2026-08-23: only 19 of 46 reclaims ever reach the 3x target, yet they carry the book — so pulling the TARGET in was strictly worse, and this protects the trade without capping them. Read the row below with it: moving all the way to breakeven was replayed and lost money at every trigger. Lab only.

params.name: exec_rec_be_keep_r
params.label: Reclaim protected stop keeps (R) of risk
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.
guide: All the way to breakeven
Leaves more risk in the market
params.desc: How FAR the stop moves when the row above arms it. 0 (default) is all the way to breakeven, which is what that row was measured with. A positive number leaves that share of the trade's own entry risk in the market, so a trade that is protected and then turns around pays part of the loss rather than none of it. MEASURED 2026-08-23: moving all the way to breakeven made the reclaim book WORSE at every trigger tested (30.00R down to 20.88R, 20.43R and 23.77R), because a stop sitting exactly at entry is inside the noise a reclaim has to survive to reach a 3x target. Must be under 1 — at 1 the stop lands back on the entry stop and does nothing while reading as switched on. Does nothing on its own. Lab only.

params.name: exec_gap_be_r
params.label: Gap re-entry moves to breakeven at (R)
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not FVG in zone, so nothing reads this.
guide: Never moves the stop
Protects the trade earlier
params.desc: When a gap re-entry's stop moves to protect the trade, measured on how far price has gone its way as a multiple of the trade's own risk. -1 (default) means never move the stop, which is what this trade did before this row existed. Each entry method owns its own stop rule and nothing else is consulted, so turning this on cannot move any other method's stop and no other method's setting can move this one. Before 2026-08-27 this trade read the shared row in Risk & stop instead, and that shared row could be overwritten by a later one — on a reclaim it produced a stop that moved AWAY from the market on a winning trade (measured: 99.00 back out to 98.50 at 2.5x in front). NEVER MEASURED ON: no replay has been run with this positive. Lab only.

params.name: exec_gap_be_keep_r
params.label: Gap re-entry protected stop keeps (R) of risk
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not FVG in zone, so nothing reads this.

Leaves more risk in the market

guide: Never moves the stop
Protects the trade earlier
params.desc: The same rule, owned by the re-entry that arms off a structure shift. -1 (default) means never move the stop, which is what this trade did before this row existed. Each entry method owns its own stop rule and nothing else is consulted, so turning this on cannot move any other method's stop and no other method's setting can move this one. Before 2026-08-27 this trade read the shared row in Risk & stop instead, and that shared row could be overwritten by a later one — on a reclaim it produced a stop that moved AWAY from the market on a winning trade (measured: 99.00 back out to 98.50 at 2.5x in front). NEVER MEASURED ON: no replay has been run with this positive. Lab only.

params.name: exec_shift_be_keep_r
params.label: Shift re-entry protected stop keeps (R) of risk
params.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Structure shift, so nothing reads this.
guide: All the way to breakeven
Leaves more risk in the market
params.desc: How FAR that stop moves when the row above arms it. 0 (default) is all the way to breakeven. A positive number leaves that share of the trade's own entry risk in the market, so a trade that is protected and then turns around pays part of the loss rather than none of it. Must be under 1 — at 1 the stop lands back on the entry stop and does nothing while reading as switched on. Does nothing on its own. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_require
params.label: Secondary needs the first trade to have…
params.disable_note: No effect under Reclaim Entry — that trigger asks its own version of this question, in the group above.
params.desc: What the first (15-minute) trade on that setup must have done before a re-entry is allowed. Breakeven (default) = it reached TP1. Any close = it traded and is now closed, win or lose. Stopped only = it was stopped out without reaching TP1 — the case where your stop gets swept and price then runs without you. None = no first trade required. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_stop
params.label: Re-entry stop sits at
params.disable_note: No effect under Reclaim Entry — its stop comes from its own row in the group above.
params.desc: Where a re-entry's stop goes. 0.886 (default) is the same level the first trade stops at. Shift leg is the original rule and only works with the Structure shift trigger, which is the only one that creates a fast-feed move to measure — pairing it with the gap trigger is refused rather than quietly substituted. Swing low uses the last confirmed swing on the fill clock; 1.0 is the start of the leg. MEASURED, and this is not a detail: on the 29 October 2025 case the same entry stopped at the gap's own edge was a loss two minutes later, and stopped 98 cents lower under the swing it ran to both targets for +16R. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_tp_r
params.label: Re-entry's first target, in R
params.disable_note: No effect under Reclaim Entry — its first target comes from its own row in the group above.
params.desc: Where a re-entry takes its first profit, measured as a multiple of its own risk. 1.25 (default) puts that first rung on the re-entry's own scale and leaves the later targets alone; how much banks there is set by "Re-entry banks this % at TP1". -1 uses the same 15-minute target the first trade uses, which was the rule until 20 August 2026. MEASURED over 7.9 years with the gap trigger on: without a rung of its own most re-entries finish flat — price moves in your favour and the breakeven stop takes you out before a 15-minute target is reached. Every rung from 0.5 to 2 was replayed and 1.25 won on the total with its single best trade removed. It also brings the move-to-breakeven point closer, so read it together with the banking percentage. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_tp1_pct
params.label: Re-entry banks this % at TP1
params.disable_note: No effect under Reclaim Entry — how much it banks comes from its own row in the group above.
params.desc: How much of a re-entry is banked at its first target, separately from the first trade. 50 (default) takes half off and runs the rest. -1 uses the same setting as everything else, which ships at nothing off — the rule until 20 August 2026. MEASURED over 7.9 years: with nothing banked, 15 of 54 re-entries finished flat; banking half left none flat, 30 winners and 24 losers, and took the leg less its single best trade from -0.4R to +7.2R. It cuts the one big winner by the same proportion, which is the trade being made. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_tp2_min_x
params.label: Re-entry's second target — how much further out than the first
guide: Off — the second target stays wherever the swing put it
Pushes the second target further away
params.desc: Stops a re-entry's two targets coming out BACKWARDS. The first target is a multiple of the trade's own risk while the second stays the 15-minute swing level it was armed on, so nothing keeps the first the nearer of the two. MEASURED 2026-08-25 over 93 re-entries: 36 came out flipped and 32 had their second target sitting INSIDE the first, one as close as 0.198 times the risk — which is noise rather than a sign the move has extended. -1 (default) is off. A positive number is the least the second target may be, as a multiple of the first one's distance from entry; the swing level still wins whenever it is already further out, so this only ever pushes a target away and never pulls one in. It reads on BOTH halves of the re-entry, which is why it sits in the shared group: the rule is a statement about the ladder, and the code applies it to every re-entry whatever armed it. MEASURED 2026-08-25: only the gap half ever comes out flipped (27 of 44), while all 47 reclaim re-entries were already in order — so on that half this only ever pushes an already-ordered target further out. It does NOT move where profit banks — the second target takes nothing off on the shipped ladder, so all that changes is when the stop lifts to the first target's price and the runner trail takes over. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_tp2_x
params.label: Re-entry's second target — set it as a multiple of the first
guide: Off — the second target stays on the swing level
Places the second target further out
params.warn: Cuts the worst drawdown at every setting measured, but three re-entries lose their only breakeven trigger and turn small wins into full losses. Ships off.
params.desc: REPLACES a re-entry's second target instead of only flooring it. The first target is a multiple of the trade's own risk while the second stays the 15-minute swing level it was armed on, so the two are measured by different rulers and the second can land nearer than the first. -1 (default) is off and the swing level stands. A positive number places the second target at that multiple of the first one's distance from entry, on EVERY re-entry, so the two are always in order. The difference from the floor setting above is direction: the floor only ever pushes a target further away and lets the swing level win when it is already out there, while this one also pulls IN a target that ran to nearly seven times the trade's risk. It does NOT move where profit banks — the second target takes nothing off on the shipped ladder, so what changes is when the stop lifts to the first target's price and hands the rest to the trail. That cuts both ways: on a trade whose swing level was the NEARER of the two, moving it out delays the point where the trade becomes unloseable. Lab only. MEASURED 2026-08-25 over 6.5 years on gold, PU Prime ECN with real fills, commission and swap: off = 139.09R at 53.68% worst drawdown; 1.1x = 142.83R at 47.95%; 1.25x = 142.87R at 47.95%; 1.5x = 141.09R at 49.02%; 2x = 140.29R at 50.67%; 2.5x = 139.79R at 51.11%. Every setting tested cut the worst drawdown, and the tighter the multiple the more it cut — that is the reason to use it. The extra money is small: about 4R over six and a half years off 15 trades. At 3x and above a re-entry starts holding long enough to block the setups behind it and the run becomes a different set of trades (237 and 235 instead of 246), so those are not like-for-like and are not quoted here. It has a real cost: three trades whose swing level was the nearer of the two rungs lose the only thing that moved their stop to breakeven, and each goes from a small win to a full loss.

params.name: exec_sec_retrace
params.label: Secondary entry retrace
params.disable_note: No effect — only the Structure shift trigger retraces a leg. The other two rest their order at a level instead: the gap uses the first trade's own price, the reclaim uses the deep edge.
params.desc: How deep the re-entry waits before its order fills. 0 enters straight away on the signal. The stop sits in the same place either way, so entering earlier means a wider stop, a smaller position and less room to the targets. Lab only.

params.name: show_div
params.label: Track RSI divergence (REQUIRED — arms setups + veto)
params.desc: Finds momentum running out - price makes a new extreme and RSI does not. Entries need this on.

params.name: div_rsi_len
params.label: RSI length
params.desc: The momentum lookback. 14 is standard. Shorter reacts faster and finds more signals.
guide: Twitchier RSI, more divergences
Smoother RSI, fewer but cleaner

params.name: div_pivot_len
params.label: Pivot width (bars)
params.desc: How many bars either side of a turn confirm it. This is also the delay — nothing can print until that many bars after the turn. Wider means fewer and cleaner signals.
guide: Confirms sooner, more noise
Confirms later, only real pivots

params.name: div_valid_bars
params.label: Divergence valid for (bars)
params.desc: How long a divergence keeps counting once it prints.
guide: Expires fast
Stays live longer

params.name: div_veto
params.label: Veto setups on extreme/divergence
params.desc: On = block a long while a bearish divergence is live or momentum is very overbought, and the mirror for shorts.

params.name: exec_respect_veto
params.label: Respect divergence/extreme veto
params.desc: On = entries obey the veto. The veto itself is switched on in the RSI divergence section.

params.name: div_extreme_ob
params.label: Extreme overbought
params.desc: Momentum at or above this counts as extremely overbought, which blocks longs. Higher blocks less often.
guide: Vetoes longs more often
Only vetoes at a true extreme

params.name: div_extreme_os
params.label: Extreme oversold
params.desc: Momentum at or below this counts as extremely oversold, which blocks shorts. Lower blocks less often.
guide: Only vetoes at a true extreme
Vetoes shorts more often

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-17:00 NY)
params.desc: On = no new entries in the last hour before the daily close, so a trade cannot be gapped out over the break.

params.name: flat_by_close
params.label: Flat by close
params.desc: Close everything before the daily close instead of holding overnight. Off by default, and that was tested: holding makes far more money, because the few trades that run overnight are the big winners and the overnight fee is tiny by comparison.

params.name: flat_by_close_min
params.label: Flatten this early
params.desc: How many minutes before the daily close to force everything flat.
guide: Hold closer to the bell
Exit earlier, more of the close avoided

params.name: exec_htf_weekly
params.label: Weekly bias requirement
params.desc: Whether the weekly trend has to agree with the trade. Ignore = no filter.
guide: Ignore = no filter, trade every setup
Must agree = only with the weekly trend

params.name: exec_htf_daily
params.label: Daily bias requirement
params.desc: The same four choices, judged on the daily trend. Ignore = off.

params.name: exec_htf_exhaust_only
params.label: Only fade HTF exhaustion, not breakouts
params.desc: On = skip a reversal that fights a fresh higher-timeframe breakout, while still taking one that fades an exhausted move.

params.name: exec_htf_source
params.label: HTF exhaustion source
params.desc: Which higher timeframe the breakout check reads. Weekly blocks the fewest trades.

params.name: exec_scratch_r
params.label: Scratch band
params.desc: Reporting only — it never changes a trade. A trade that finishes this close to breakeven is counted as a scratch instead of a win or a loss. It matters because this bot scratches a lot.
guide: Fewer trades called scratch
More near-breakeven trades called scratch

params.name: alert_resting_fib
params.label: Announce a resting limit at fib
params.desc: Reporting only — it never changes a trade, and the order is still placed the moment the setup arms. It decides WHEN the signals channel tells you a limit is pending: price has to retrace this far back down the leg first. At the default the order is announced once price has given back 23.6% of the move, instead of the moment it is placed — which can be hours and tens of dollars before price could reach it. Must stay under 0.5, because every fill happens at 0.5 or deeper and the message has to go out before any trade can.
guide: Told sooner, further from the entry
Told later, closer to the entry

params.name: fill_model
params.label: Fill model
params.desc: How fills are priced. Bar matches the TradingView chart and charges nothing, which is the mode used to check the two against each other. Tick uses real bid and ask prices with real costs. Use tick for any number you want to trust.

params.name: account_profile
params.label: Account profile
params.desc: Whose costs to charge in tick mode. vantage_demo is the broker the backtests are measured on, so results line up with the TradingView chart. The puprime ones are the live broker, kept for reference. Ignored in bar mode.

params.name: symbol
params.label: Broker symbol
params.desc: The symbol the price data is pulled from. Vantage gold is XAUUSD, with no suffix. Ignored in bar mode.

params.name: exec_recovery
params.label: Loss recovery trades
params.desc: ⚠ The result this switch prints is wrong in BOTH directions, so do not read it as what the rule is worth. After this bot loses a trade, it takes a smaller trade the other way to win the loss back. But the recovery is worked out afterwards, over the main book once that book has already finished. Each recovery trade is sized off a balance holding every main trade that had closed by then, so that half is real - what is missing is the way back: the main trades never see the recovery profit, so it sits beside the equity curve instead of lifting it and never compounds. That UNDERSTATES the rule on a long run. Pulling the other way, nothing here shares one risk budget, so a recovery can never shrink or block a main trade the way it would on a real account - and that FLATTERS it. Which of the two wins is not a detail: measured on one balance under one budget, the rule loses money at the risk cap this bot already runs, and only pays when given risk the main bot is not using. Run backtest/tools/recovery_stack.py for the real answer, and read strategies/python/loss_recovery/CLAUDE.md before quoting any figure this switch produces. Lab only - this is not on the TradingView chart and it has never been traded live.
guide: ⚠ Answers a different question than the one you are asking - see the description
Adds a second, smaller set of trades to the book
Off = the bot trades only its own setups

params.name: exec_recovery_risk_frac
params.label: ↳ Size vs a normal trade
params.desc: How big a recovery trade is next to a normal one. 0.25 means a quarter of the usual risk.
guide: Bigger recovery trades, and a bigger drawdown with them
Smaller, safer, and worth less

params.name: exec_recovery_lock_at_r
params.label: ↳ Secure the trade at
params.desc: How far the recovery trade has to travel in your favour before the stop is moved up. 1 is the point where the original loss has been paid back.
guide: Waits longer before protecting the trade
Protects sooner, and gets stopped out more

params.name: exec_recovery_lock_to_r
params.label: ↳ Move the stop to
params.desc: Where the stop goes once it moves. 1 banks the recovery. 0 is plain breakeven, which protects you from losing but does not bank the thing you entered for.
guide: Locks in more, and is taken out by a smaller wobble
Locks in less, and gives the trade more room

params.name: exec_recovery_soft_stop_r
params.label: ↳ Cut early at
params.desc: Give up once the trade is this far against you, instead of waiting for the full stop. 0 leaves the full stop in place. This is the only setting here that makes a losing recovery trade cost less.
guide: Sits through more of the stop
Cuts sooner: smaller losses, but fewer winners survive

params.name: exec_recovery_both_dirs
params.label: ↳ Take both directions
params.desc: Whether to take the recovery trade whichever way it points. Turning this off keeps only the direction that happened to win in the past, which is a decision made after seeing the answer.

params.name: exec_recovery_max_days
params.label: ↳ Give up after
params.desc: Close a recovery trade that has gone nowhere after this many days. A backstop — most trades finish in about four days. It exists because trades left open for months pay a lot of overnight interest.
guide: Holds losing trades longer and pays more overnight interest
Cuts stale trades sooner

params.name: exec_sh_block_from
params.label: Block entries from this New York hour
params.desc: Start of an extra no-entry window, in New York hours. -1 on both this and the one below means off, which is the default. Only read when the short-hold variant is on.

params.name: exec_sh_block_to
params.label: ...until this New York hour
params.desc: End of that window, exclusive. It may wrap past midnight. Set both to -1 to switch it off. Only read when the short-hold variant is on.

params.name: exec_sh_max_depth
params.label: Refuse an entry deeper than this fib
params.desc: Skips a setup whose entry would sit deeper into the pullback than this level. 1.0 refuses nothing, which is the default: capping at 0.702 was measured to remove five trades and cost 2.1R. Only read when the short-hold variant is on.

params.name: exec_sh_tp1_pct
params.label: How much comes off at that target
params.desc: 100 takes the whole position off and leaves no runner, which is the point of the variant. Less than 100 hands the remainder back to the normal runner. Only read when the short-hold variant is on.

params.name: exec_sh_tp_r
params.label: Close the position at this many R
params.desc: Where the whole trade comes off, measured in multiples of what it is risking. Best of the ones tested; below 1.5 nothing works. Only read when the short-hold variant is on.

params.name: exec_short_hold
params.label: Short-hold variant

options.on: Bank a fixed R and close

params.desc: Trades the same setups a different way: closes the whole position at a set multiple of risk instead of banking a little and riding the rest. Measured MARGINAL - it removes almost every scratch and earns about half as much. A switch to experiment with, not a leg to run.

params.name: exec_min_atr_pct
params.label: Minimum market volatility (% of price)
params.desc: Skip a setup when the market is barely moving. Measured as the average 15-minute range as a percent of price. 0 turns it off. This is NOT the minimum stop distance above: that one asks whether the stop is far enough away to size against, this one asks whether the market is moving at all. A wide stop in a dead market clears that floor and is still refused here. Higher refuses more setups.
guide: Nothing is refused
Refuses real trades, not just dead ones
